issues.description: The manuscript’s central claim is stronger than the evidence. The study does not demonstrate an absence of causal understanding; it shows no increase in a narrow post-task measure and later acknowledges that participants performed above chance and used useful intuitions. The data therefore support, at most, that full multidimensional explicit/verbalizable understanding was not necessary in this task, not that causal understanding was absent or unnecessary.
issues.quote: Here, we show that a physical artifact becomes progressively optimized across generations of social learners in the absence of explicit causal understanding.

issues.description: The conclusions are extended from a highly simplified, low-dimensional wheel task with immediate feedback to ‘complex technologies’ and archaeological inference. This extrapolation is not justified by the design. Real technologies are typically higher-dimensional, noisier, socially embedded, and learned over much longer timescales.
issues.quote: These results indicate that complex technologies need not result from enhanced causal reasoning but instead can emerge from the accumulation of improvements made across generations.

issues.description: The operationalization of ‘understanding’ is a 10-item pairwise comparison task on isolated one-factor contrasts. That tests selected comparative predictions, not integrated causal reasoning about the full tradeoff participants had to optimize in the task. A participant could succeed on these items via simple heuristics without possessing the multidimensional causal model the paper claims to measure, and conversely could understand some aspects of the task not captured by these items.
issues.quote: Participants’ understanding was evaluated by presenting them with pairs of wheels that differed in their configurations, and asking them to estimate how long each wheel would take to reach the bottom of the rails... The test comprised 10 pairs of wheels: 5 in which wheels varied in their moment of inertia, 5 in which wheels varied in the position of their centre of mass.

issues.description: The ‘theory’ manipulation is heavily constrained and framed as a performance rule. The fixed sentence stem and 340-character limit make it difficult to communicate richer causal explanations or nuanced multidimensional tradeoffs. As a result, null effects cannot be generalized to ‘causal model transmission’ broadly; the study only tests transmission of very brief heuristic statements.
issues.quote: Theories had to be less than 340 characters long and always started with “The wheel covers the distance faster when...”.

issues.description: The ‘Configurations + Theory’ condition differs from the comparison condition in at least two ways: participants receive a theory and also must generate/write a theory. Writing a theory can itself alter attention, reflection, encoding, and later test performance. Any treatment difference therefore cannot be attributed specifically to theory transmission.
issues.quote: In the “Configurations + Theory” treatment (n =70), participants additionally received the previous participant’s theory about the physical system. Participants were asked to write their theory before the test phase was completed.

issues.description: The experimenter physically positioned the weights on the wheel, and data collection was not blind to condition. Because setup and release of a physical apparatus can be affected by subtle handling differences, lack of blinding introduces avoidable risk of expectancy effects or differential treatment across conditions.
issues.quote: Once the configuration was confirmed by the participant, the experimenter positioned the weights on the physical wheel accordingly... Data collection and was not performed blind to the conditions of the experiments.

issues.description: Trials in which the wheel did not descend are handled inconsistently across analyses: they are partly avoided by restricting the dataset in some analyses, but coded as speed = 0 in another. These are not equivalent estimands. Excluding or minimizing failures can bias performance upward, while coding failure as zero conflates descent probability with conditional speed. A two-part/hurdle approach or consistent prespecified handling was needed.
issues.quote: Analysis 1 ... Data were restricted to participants’ last two trials in order to limit the occurrence of wheels that did not descend in the dataset... Analysis 3 ... Wheels that did not go down were attributed a speed of 0. Data were restricted to participants’ last two trials in order to limit the occurrence of wheels that did not descend in the dataset.

issues.description: Understanding scores are bounded discrete counts, yet they were analyzed with a linear model. A binomial/logistic or ordinal/count model would better reflect the measurement scale and boundary constraints, especially because the paper’s main claim rests on a null effect for understanding.
issues.quote: We fitted a linear model with “Score” as the outcome variable

issues.description: The manuscript states that final model specification was chosen after comparing several candidate models based on fit to observed data. This creates researcher degrees of freedom and weakens the confirmatory status of the reported results, especially because the criteria and candidate set are not described here.
issues.quote: The final model specification was selected after comparing several candidate models based on fit to the observed data.

issues.description: A key preregistered analysis was changed after the planned model did not converge. The authors aggregated inertia and centre-of-mass scores, thereby changing the estimand and potentially masking theoretically meaningful shifts between the two dimensions. This is especially consequential because the paper’s central conclusion is that understanding did not improve.
issues.quote: As a result, the preregistered model did not converge so we ran our analysis on aggregated score and removed the terms associated the variable “Physical Principle” in the reported model.

issues.description: The reported Generation × Treatment interval for understanding excludes zero, which under the manuscript’s own interval-based logic is evidence of an interaction. Yet the text concludes that the analyses do not support an effect of theory transmission on understanding. This is an interpretive inconsistency in the main results.
issues.quote: participants in the very last generation had a slightly better understanding when they had inherited a theory (Treatment 95% CI: (-2.54, 0.31), mean = -1.14; Generation x Treatment 95% CI: (0.03, 0.81), mean = 0.44, Figure 2.B). Thus, these analyses do not provide substantial support for the idea that the transmission of explicit causal theories affects wheel optimization and individual understanding.

issues.description: The study makes strong null-leaning claims (e.g., that theory transmission has no noticeable effect), but no formal power or precision analysis was conducted. Because chain is the independent unit, 14 chains per treatment may be insufficient to rule out practically meaningful effects, especially interactions.
issues.quote: No statistical methods were used to pre-determine sample sizes but our sample sizes (i.e. number of independent chains) are larger than those reported in previous publications30,31.

issues.description: The manuscript makes causal claims about what inheriting different kinds of theories does to exploration and understanding, but participants were not randomly assigned to theory type. Theory content arose endogenously from previous participants and may be confounded with chain history, predecessor ability, or other unmeasured factors. The subsequent subgroup comparisons are observational.
issues.quote: These results suggest that the understanding patterns observed in participants who received unidimensional theories is likely the result of the canalizing effect of theory transmission on exploration.

issues.description: The exploratory mechanism claims rest on very small subgroups, especially the ‘full theory’ group (N = 6), and on post hoc categorization. Such small Ns make the subgroup patterns unstable and highly sensitive to a few observations.
issues.quote: Of the 56 participants who inherited a theory (all participants in the “Configurations + Theory” treatment except first-generation participants), 15 inherited an inertia-related theory, 17 inherited a centre-of-mass-related theory, 6 inherited a full theory and 18 inherited diverse, irrelevant theories.

issues.description: The Bayesian analyses are underreported. The manuscript does not provide priors, number of chains/iterations, warmup, convergence diagnostics, posterior predictive checks, or the criteria used for model comparison. Without these details, the analyses are difficult to evaluate or reproduce.
issues.quote: We ran a series of Bayesian multi-level models in R 32.  Models were fitted using map2stan in the rethinking package 33 and 95% credible intervals were used to make inferences.

issues.description: Absolute speed values are reported as if based on 1 meter, but the apparatus description states the timing switches were 92 cm apart. This inconsistency affects the reported speeds and any derived claims about percentage optimization or proximity to the maximum possible speed.
issues.quote: The average wheel speed (calculated as 1m/descent time) increased across generations

issues.description: This sentence makes a direct empirical generalization to mixed-gender collaborative settings, but the study used only sex-segregated chains and collected no mixed-gender data. The claim is unsupported by the design.
issues.quote: These findings generalize beyond the single-sex chain compositions used here, suggesting cultural transmission operates similarly in mixed-gender collaborative settings.

issues.description: The participant pool is a narrow WEIRD sample of French university students. Claims about human technological evolution, cumulative culture, or archaeological inference should be tempered accordingly; the social learning strategies and intuitions observed here may not generalize broadly.
issues.quote: we asked successive ‘cultural generations’ of participants (French university students) to optimize a physical system

issues.description: The manuscript treats the cultural niche hypothesis as predicting no increase in understanding. That is a stronger claim than the theory requires. Cumulative cultural evolution can be compatible with partial, local, or increasing individual understanding; the theory does not logically imply a flat understanding trajectory.
issues.quote: The cultural niche hypothesis predicts that the speed of the wheel will increase with generations, while participants’ understanding of the system will not improve over generations (preregistered hypothesis 1).

issues.description: Participants were explicitly incentivized to help their successor, which likely encourages teaching-oriented or cooperative transmission strategies. That means the study tests a mixture of cumulative cultural transmission and deliberate pedagogical behavior, not just selective retention of successful variants.
issues.quote: Participants were informed that their last two trials would be transmitted to the next participant in the chain, and that their reward depended both on their own performance and on the performance of the next participant in the chain.

issues.description: The discussion argues against concerns that poor intuitive physics results are artifacts of impoverished picture-based stimuli. But understanding was still assessed via displayed pairs of wheels rather than solely through live interaction with the physical object. The study therefore does not fully eliminate the measurement concern it claims to answer.
issues.quote: our results show that incomplete representations commonly emerge even when individuals directly observe and modify an actual physical object.

issues.description: All participants saw the same 10 test items in the same order. Without counterbalancing, order effects, fatigue, or progressive adoption of response heuristics can contaminate the understanding scores.
issues.quote: All participants were exposed to the same 10 pairs of wheels in the same order.

issues.description: Chains were sex-segregated, but the manuscript does not report how male and female chains were distributed across treatments or whether sex was tested as a moderator. Because chain is the unit of independence, imbalance could confound treatment comparisons.
issues.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one condition of the experiment and one sex-segregated chain.

issues.description: The analyses are described as Bayesian, yet the results report ‘95% Confidence Intervals’ for model parameters while also using HPDIs elsewhere. This mixes inferential frameworks and makes the meaning of the reported intervals unclear.
issues.quote: Results confirm these predictions. The average wheel speed (calculated as 1m/descent time) increased across generations (Generation 95% Confidence Intervals: (1.58, 9.02), mean = 5.37 m/h, Figure 2.A)

issues.description: The manuscript reports ‘71% optimization’ without explaining the calculation, and that figure is not transparent from the reported speeds. If the percentage is normalized relative to a baseline or payoff transformation, the formula should be stated explicitly.
issues.quote: Given that the maximum possible speed was about 154 m/h, these results indicate an optimization of 71% after only four cultural generations.
